title: Campaigns OS Runtime Recipe v1
description: Validates a runtime-readiness recipe document: the small, fixed, declarative description of how a checkout of this repository at one commit becomes a usable installed runtime. It is data, never code — a consumer executes only the commands enumerated here, never a free-form command assembled from repository data. A consumer that recognizes v1 accepts and preserves unknown additive properties without interpreting them, while required fields, known types, and safety-critical enums stay strict: an unrecognized recipe_kind, recipe_revision, network policy, output-check kind, or disagreement disposition is a fail-closed refusal, not a value to guess at. recipe_kind names what an installed consumer must already understand in order to execute the document at all, so a new kind requires a consumer release before the recipe is publishable; recipe_revision re-parameterises fields an existing consumer already understands, so a consumer accepts any revision inside the major line its kind declares.

_growth_note.description: Free-text note on what to do when a declared bound is genuinely reached. Not consumed.

recipe_kind.description: Safety-critical. The enumerated set of recipe kinds this schema version defines. A document naming any other kind fails closed: an installed consumer cannot execute a kind it was not released knowing.

recipe_revision.description: Safety-critical. Semver, and its major MUST be 1 for every kind this schema version defines. A revision re-parameterises fields the consumer already understands — accepted version bounds, timeout values, the enumerated input set, the expected output inventory. A major other than 1 is a shape change wearing a revision's clothes and fails closed.

refusal_reason_code.description: The single stable reason code a consumer emits when this recipe refuses. One code, so a refusal is always attributable to the recipe rather than to whatever step happened to notice.

fail_closed.description: Safety-critical. Every field in this document is normative and enforced. There is no advisory mode: a bound not worth enforcing is dropped, never demoted.

unperformable_check_disposition.description: Safety-critical. A declared check that cannot be performed — the measurement is absent, non-finite, or the check itself errored — counts as FAILED, never as skipped. Carried over from contracts/orientation-limits.v1.json, where an absent measurement counts as exceeded for the same reason.

preconditions.description: Conditions that must already hold before any step runs. All are booleans fixed to true: a precondition a document could switch off is not a precondition.

field.description: The dotted path in the target's package.json whose declared value this recipe was written against.

observed.description: The exact value of that field at the commit this revision was authored against. A checker compares the target's live value to this string; any difference is a disagreement.

on_disagreement.description: Safety-critical. What happens when the contract's declared range and the target's declared engines disagree. Only refuse is defined: an accept-with-warning path produces a build made under conditions nobody approved plus a log line nobody reads.

cache_ownership.description: Safety-critical. Who owns the package cache. The cache is an optimisation and never a correctness input, so it belongs to the consumer profile rather than to the operator's ambient environment.

per_step.description: Network policy keyed by step id. Every step in steps[] must appear here; a step with no declared policy is unbounded network access nobody approved.

steps.description: The ordered, exhaustive command set. A consumer executes these and nothing else.

files.description: The complete, explicitly enumerated input set, repository-root-relative. Enumerated rather than globbed on purpose: the compiler's resolved file set is not the config's include globs, and a fingerprint derived from the globs would silently cover a subset.

committed.description: Safety-critical. The output directory is a build product, never a committed artifact, so no baseline hash for its contents can exist in this repository. Verification is self-consistency, not comparison against a published expectation.

module_source_root.description: The input prefix that output paths are derived relative to.

expected_module_derivation.description: How the expected output inventory is derived from the enumerated input set. A derivation, not a second list: a duplicated inventory is a literal that can rot out of step with the inputs that produce it.

checks.description: Every declared check is mandatory. There is no optional check: an optional check is an advisory bound under another name.

bounds.description: Enforced resource bounds. Each carries its unit, what it applies to, and a rationale stating the measured baseline and the resulting headroom, so a number is never mistaken for physics.

scripts.description: The exact text of every package script this recipe depends on, at the commit the revision was authored against. A consumer-side checker compares the target's live script text to these strings; any difference is a change to what the recipe would execute, and it fails until the recipe is revised.

install_script_dependencies.description: Every resolved dependency that declares an install script, as recorded in the lockfile. Enumerated so a newly introduced install script is a gate failure rather than a silent addition to what would run if the suppressing flag were ever dropped.

target_expectations.description: What the recipe assumes about the target at the commit this revision was authored against. Machine-comparable on purpose: the assumptions a recipe makes about its target are the part most likely to rot, and prose cannot be diffed.

browser_qa.description: Whether a generation prepared by this recipe can run browser QA. False for every v1 recipe: running install with lifecycle scripts disabled also suppresses the browser-download step of the browser automation dependency, so a prepared generation can build and type-check but cannot drive a browser. "Runtime ready" must not be read as "can run QA".

range.description: Human-readable range, for documentation. The machine comparison uses min_inclusive / max_exclusive / accepted_majors, never this string.

verified.description: Exact versions this range was measured against.

policy.description: Safety-critical. allowlist permits exactly the hosts in hosts[]; deny permits none. There is no allow-all value, and an unrecognized value fails closed.

integrity_source.description: What bounds WHICH bytes are acceptable, as distinct from where they may come from.

id.description: Safety-critical. The enumerated step identities a v1 consumer understands.

executable.description: Safety-critical. The only package manager a v1 recipe may name. A different one is a new kind, because the consumer would have to understand new argv.

args.description: The exact argv, in order. A consumer executes this verbatim and never assembles or interpolates arguments.

lifecycle_scripts.description: Safety-critical. Dependency and pre/post lifecycle scripts do not run in any v1 step. This is why the build is an explicit contracted step rather than a side effect of installing.

timeout_bound.description: The key in bounds{} that bounds this step.

kind.description: Safety-critical. The enumerated check kinds a v1 consumer can perform. A new kind of check is a new recipe kind: an installed consumer cannot perform a check it was not released knowing how to perform, and per unperformable_check_disposition it must then report FAILED rather than skip.

depth.description: Only meaningful for module_import_smoke. shallow imports the package entry module and lets it load its own graph; deep imports every emitted module individually.

detects.description: The failure modes this check is responsible for catching. Together the checks must cover absent, stale, extra, and corrupt output; staleness in particular is invisible to every output-side check, because stale output is internally consistent.
